design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (returns_and_exchanges). Revision 3 (policy-task audit rounds 1 and 2 closed; finding-by-finding closure in the difficulty worklog).
[Draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5, 5, 4, 6]; assigned: return shipping fee 6, shoebox fee 5, Instant Exchange hold 5, final card refund 4.
[Scope] Task 0 holds credit entry, restocking fee, spent-credit card charge and courtesy extension. Claimed here, disjoint: returns_ext_return_shipping_fee (withhold_return_shipping_fee_e68e1eec), returns_ext_shoebox_fee (assess_box_fee_f48699d7), returns_ext_final_card_refund (pay_final_card_refund_b5173030), returns_ext_exchange_hold (place_exchange_hold_2c1506d4, owner=user). Together the two tasks cover all eight policies.
[Why a good test] The customer asks only to finish an Instant Exchange stuck at the card hold. The hold's rule carries 'An Instant Exchange card hold against an order is placed only after every return on that order that has passed inspection carries its final-settlement refund.' The agent must find the same order's inspected Standard Return X1 (625bb104-5dda-45ca-a1e2-ffc4dc379994) with only its credit entry, read the final refund's two sentences (a Standard Return carries a return shipping fee and the sneakers' shoebox came back damaged), book both fees, pay the refund and hand the hold to the cardholder.
[Problem tree] root returns_ext_exchange_hold <-state_gate- returns_ext_final_card_refund <-value_input- returns_ext_return_shipping_fee and <-value_input- returns_ext_shoebox_fee. 3 prerequisite problems, 2 value_input edges, all state form with a single writer each. The two refund sentences are scoped to return types that carry those fees (Quality Issue Returns and exchanges never wait on them).
[Unmet at frozen_time] X1 status inspected; its only entry is the credit ee7bb3fc-c277-40e2-9b44-d5d66fe07a43; inspection shows the sneakers' shoebox damaged/used as shipper; return method scheduled_pickup; no fee or refund entry.
[Topological order] fees (steps 14 and 16, commuting: swapped order gives the same refund 126.93) -> refund (18) -> hold (22, customer).
[Sensitivity run] skip return shipping fee: refund 126.93 -> 129.40; skip shoebox fee: refund -> 133.68.
[Factor card] Return shipping fee (scored 2.47; baseline 9.95): two labels (method; the closing formula now names the number of labels), Silver >=60 months 0.75 (loyalty), Standard Annual 0.8, accepted share 1/2 (method), quick reduction 2.00, Missing Item Claim reduction 1.50 (claims). Shoebox fee (scored 6.75; baseline 10.00): damaged box 5.00, 12-month spend 1166.40 -> 0.6 (loyalty), premium pair x1.5 (parameter) 4.50, return rate measure (method, loyalty: Silver is measured by value, 261.00 reversed over 1166.40 earned in the last 12 calendar months = 0.224, at least 0.2 -> x1.5; the baseline count measure, 3 reversals over 3 orders placed = 1.00, gives x2 and 9.00), frequency x1.5 (parameter) 4.50; ceiling = the pair's net unit price paid read from the order. Final card refund (scored 126.93; baseline 125.18): not_as_pictured share 0.5, pro-rata basis (method), Next Business Day refunded at the Expedited list fee, NJ shipping tax (method); never above the card's refundable remainder (562.53). Hold (scored 101.57; baseline 202.76): value basis (method: price paid for a promoted line; reference price for an adjusted line; list otherwise) 169.29, NJ footwear no tax (method, multi-source) 105.38, Silver 0.9 (loyalty) 112.86, e-Gift Card security 0.75 (credit) 135.43, prompt 0.95 106.92. Near-misses: the scarf refunded by the claim stays in booked accessories; net 134.40 below 150 while booked 168.00 is above; the 2025-08-18 reversal and its 2025-07-30 order fall outside the 12 rate months.
[Overrides declared] shoebox amount clause; method fee clause and 'waivers do not add up' (closing formula with the number of labels); refund amount and original-shipping clauses (card refundable cap kept); Instant Exchange consent/amount clause (the hold is placed by the cardholder personally). Waiver tiers are read as held since the authorization date.
[Base-invariant card] fees: inspected_only (X1 inspected), returns_evt_method_fee policy_scope; refund: refund_after_inspection, one_payment_per_stage_tender, returns_evt_gift_return policy_scope (order not a gift); hold: consent kept as the cardholder's own act; card tender and value below 400.00.
[Business-object card] X1 lines: sneakers accepted with fee (box), dress rejected; the shoebox fee keys on the sneaker line; the method fee and refund key on X1; the hold keys on Y (fef5233c-178c-4c65-90d9-dd51bf1488c9). Older settled returns feed loyalty reversals only.
[Persona] Calm researcher on lunch break; volunteers only the stuck exchange; identity on request; passive consent to settle the earlier return and to the hold; runs the hold with the reference and amount the agent states.
[Standard solution] Locate (phone), verify (email + ZIP), read returns, all return lines, settlements, orders, lines, payments, membership, ledger, Unlimited, claims and claim entries; withhold the return shipping fee 2.47 and the shoebox fee 6.75; pay the final card refund 126.93; read stored value; hand over the hold of 101.57.
[Verification] Handling-time replay through the real tools reproduces every value; gates logged in the difficulty worklog.
user_scenario: You are Joelle Ingram, a 33-year-old UX researcher in Hoboken, New Jersey, calm and organised, calling on your lunch break. This morning you started an Instant Exchange on the Marlowe & Finch website for the Harlow Leather Chelsea Boots from your late-September order, swapping your US 8 for a US 8.5, but the site stopped at the card hold step and nothing is shipping. Your goal: get that exchange completed today so the bigger boots ship; you are fine with a temporary hold on your card as long as the agent tells you the amount, and you will do any step on your side yourself. Open with roughly: "Hi, I started an instant exchange for my Chelsea boots this morning, a half size up, but it got stuck at the card hold part. Can you help me finish it so the new pair ships?" If asked how to find your account you give your mobile number 2015550124. When the agent asks to confirm your identity you give your email joelle.ingram@gmail.com and, if a second detail is needed, your billing ZIP code 07030; you do not offer them before being asked. You do not know the exchange's reference number by heart; tell the agent to look it up. You never bring up any other return, refund, fee or claim on your own. If the agent explains that the earlier return from the same order (the sneakers and the slip dress you sent back by courier pickup) has to be settled first, you say that is fine - you were waiting for that refund anyway - and to go ahead. If the agent asks whether you agree to the hold on the card you paid the order with, you say yes. Only when the agent hands you the step to place the hold do you run it, with exactly the exchange's reference number and the amount the agent states, and you then read back the confirmation you see. If asked which card, it is the same card you paid that order with. You never suggest an amount and never question how it was worked out; if asked whether it sounds right, you say you will trust their records. Once the hold is placed and the agent confirms the new boots will ship, you thank them and end the call. If the agent says the exchange cannot go ahead, you ask once why, accept it, and end the call.

edges.condition: Every return of the exchange's order in status inspected carries a returns_refund_issued settlement entry with refund_stage final_settlement.
edges.policy_source: An Instant Exchange card hold against an order is placed only after every return on that order that has passed inspection carries its final-settlement refund.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Return X1 on the exchange's order is in status inspected and carries only its credit entry: no final-settlement refund entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 18 books a returns_refund_issued entry with refund_stage final_settlement on X1.

edges.condition: On a return whose type has return_method_fee_applies, the return carries a returns_fee_assessed settlement entry of fee type method_fee.
edges.policy_source: The final card refund on a return whose type carries a return shipping fee is fixed only after the return carries the return shipping fee entry for the method its parcel travelled by.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: X1 was charged by scheduled pickup but carries no method fee entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 14 books the method fee entry; fees on the return rise by it.

edges.condition: On a return whose type carries shoebox fees, every footwear line inspected with box condition no_original_box or original_box_damaged_or_used_as_shipper has a returns_fee_assessed entry of fee type missing_box_fee.
edges.policy_source: That refund is not paid until every footwear line whose shoebox came back missing, damaged or used as the shipping carton, on a return whose type carries shoebox fees, carries its shoebox fee entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The sneakers came back in a damaged shoebox but X1 carries no shoebox fee entry.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 16 books the shoebox fee entry; fees on the return rise by it.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two fees are parallel prerequisites of the card refund; each writes its own entry and neither reads the other (the shoebox fee reads the order's net price, the return shipping fee reads inspection entries), so either order gives the same terminal state: the replay with the fee calls swapped gives the same refund 126.93. The refund follows both (its two sentences) and the hold follows the refund (the hold's sentence).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the card refund leaves X1 without its final-settlement refund entry in the terminal state (and the hold, gated on it, should not be placed); the gold hash differs.
